examples.question_text: The continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on $[3,11]$. Find its probability density function and explain why its total area is $1$.

$X$ is uniformly distributed on $[-2,10]$. Find:
a. $P(1\le X\le5)$
b. $P(X\le4)$
c. $P(X>7)$.

A machine produces a cord length $X$, in centimetres, uniformly distributed on $[120,132]$. Find:
a. $P(128\le X\le136)$
b. $P(115\le X\le123)$
c. $P(134\le X\le138)$.
examples.solution_text:
The density is $\frac{1}{132-120}=\frac{1}{12}$ on $[120,132]$ and $0$ outside it. Use only the part of each requested interval within the support.

a. The overlapping interval is $[128,132]$.
$\begin{align*}P(128\le X\le136)&=\frac{1}{12}(132-128)\\&=\frac{1}{3}.\end{align*}$

b. The overlapping interval is $[120,123]$.
$\begin{align*}P(115\le X\le123)&=\frac{1}{12}(123-120)\\&=\frac{1}{4}.\end{align*}$

c. The interval $[134,138]$ has no overlap with $[120,132]$.
$P(134\le X\le138)=0$.

examples.derivation: Support width is 11−3=8, giving density 1/8 on [3,11] and zero otherwise. The non-negative density has total area 8×1/8=1. The diagram correctly labels the support and density; its axis break resolves the omitted horizontal range.

Support width is 10−(−2)=12. The interval probability is (5−1)/12=1/3, the lower tail is (4−(−2))/12=1/2, and the upper tail is (10−7)/12=1/4. Integrating the constant density gives the same results. Diagram coordinates consistently represent x/2, and shading marks exactly [1,5].
Support width is 132−120=12. Intersections with the support are [128,132], [120,123], and the empty set, giving probabilities 4/12=1/3, 3/12=1/4, and 0 respectively.
